#load data
```{r}
manuscript_table<-read_excel(here("output_data/summaries/combined_aquaculture_species_summaries.xlsx"),
  sheet = "Manuscript Table"  # select the sheets in the excel file
)

land_species<-read_excel(here("output_data/summaries/combined_aquaculture_species_summaries.xlsx"),
  sheet = "Land National")  # select the sheets in the excel file
  
marine_Infra<-read_excel(here("output_data/summaries/combined_aquaculture_species_summaries.xlsx"),
  sheet = "Marine Infra National")  # select the sheets in the excel file 

marine_species<-read_excel(here("output_data/summaries/combined_aquaculture_species_summaries.xlsx"),
  sheet = "Marine Infra by State")  # select the sheets in the excel file
marine_leases<-read_excel(here("output_data/summaries/combined_aquaculture_species_summaries.xlsx"),
  sheet = "Marine Lease National")  # select the sheets in the excel file
```

#Results for manuscript
```{r}
#marine infrastructure detected
# What is the number of sites that are active or have presence of infrastructure we had # 2158
marine_sites_presence<-sum(marine_Infra$n_detections)
#What is the total area of the Marine aquaculture infrastructure? We found #24.951km2
marine_infra_area<-sum(marine_Infra$total_infra_km2)

# area of all marine leases
number_marine_leases<-sum(marine_leases$n_leases)#5528
area_marine_leases<-sum(marine_leases$lease_area_km2)#961.756km2

#percentage of active leases
percent_active_leases<- as.numeric(marine_sites_presence/number_marine_leases)
#percentage of active area
percentage_area_productive<-as.numeric(marine_infra_area/area_marine_leases)



```
#text for the manuscript
```{r marine-infrastructure-text, results='asis'}
cat("
In the marine realm,", sprintf('%.2f', marine_infra_area), "km² of aquaculture 
infrastructure were detected nationally across", 
sprintf('%.0f', percent_active_leases*100), "% of the registered marine leases (", 
marine_sites_presence, "of", number_marine_leases, "), corresponding to", 
sprintf('%.1f', percentage_area_productive*100), "% of the total licensed marine 
lease area (", sprintf('%.1f', area_marine_leases), "km²). This footprint comprised 
primarily longline systems (17.97 km²; 72%) over cages (6.98 km²; 28%). All sites 
with detected infrastructure were classified as potentially active. Species 
attribution was possible for", sprintf('%.1f', 2137/marine_sites_presence*100), 
"% of sites (2,137 sites) and", sprintf('%.1f', 24.8/marine_infra_area*100), 
"% of the infrastructure area (24.8 km²), while", 
sprintf('%.1f', 21/marine_sites_presence*100), 
"% of sites (21 sites) and", sprintf('%.1f', 0.159/marine_infra_area*100), 
"% (0.159 km²) of infrastructure remained unassigned.
")
```
#land_based results
```{r}
# Read the data
national_sf <- st_read(here("output_data", "Land_Aquaculture_Vectors", 
                            "Australia_Land_Aquaculture_National.shp"))
```

#calculations and text
```{r land-infrastructure-text, results='asis'}
cat("
Land-based aquaculture infrastructure occupied", sprintf('%.2f', sum(national_sf$In_A_KM, na.rm=TRUE)), 
"km² nationally in 2021–2022, corresponding to", 
sprintf('%.1f', sum(national_sf$In_A_KM, na.rm=TRUE)/sum(national_sf$Ls_A_KM, na.rm=TRUE)*100), 
"% of the total licensed land-based lease area (", 
sprintf('%.1f', sum(national_sf$Ls_A_KM, na.rm=TRUE)), "km²), and exhibited a markedly 
uneven spatial distribution among states. Queensland accounted for the largest 
share (13.03 km², 49%), followed by South Australia (8.78 km²). Smaller footprints 
were detected in New South Wales (2 km²), the Northern Territory (1.57 km²), and 
Western Australia (1.29 km²), while Victoria (0.19 km²) and Tasmania (0.1 km²) 
had comparatively minor areas. Across the 441 land-based aquaculture sites 
identified nationally, 294 (66.7%) were classified as active and 147 (33.3%) as 
inactive (Figure 2). Species attribution was possible for 61.2% of the sites 
(270 sites) and 86.3% of the infrastructure area (22.961 km²), while 38.8% of 
the sites (171 sites) and 13.7% (3.63 km²) of the infrastructure remained unassigned.
")
```

#comparison_land_marine

```{r comparison-text, results='asis'}
cat("
Despite similar total infrastructure areas (land-based: 27.09 km²; marine: 24.95 km²), 
the two realms differed markedly in lease utilisation, site activity, and species 
attribution. Marine leases covered a smaller total licensed area (961.8 km²) than 
land-based leases (2,294.56 km²), yet both realms exhibited low infrastructure-to-lease 
ratios (marine: 2.6%; land-based: 1.5%), reflecting the large proportion of registered 
but unproductive lease area in Australian aquaculture. Infrastructure was detected at 
39% of registered marine leases (2,158 of 5,528), all classified as potentially active, 
whereas land-based detection was proportionally higher (66.7%; 294 of 441), though 
one third of land-based sites (147; 33.3%) showed no detectable infrastructure. 
Species attribution was near-complete for marine sites (99.0% of sites; 99.4% of area), 
compared to considerably lower coverage for land-based operations (61.2% of sites; 
86.3% of area), likely reflecting greater privacy constraints on land-based farm data, 
as marine leases are granted over public waters and are therefore less subject to 
land tenure and privacy restrictions
")
```
